ISSUE
Approve Purchase Order No. 20230005 with Nixon-Egli Equipment Company of
Southern California for a new 2021 demo unit Petersen TL3 Lightning Loader Grapple
Truck in an amount not to exceed $224,587.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council approve Purchase Order No. 20230005 with
Nixon-Egli Equipment Company of Southern California for a new 2021 demo unit
Petersen TL3 Lightning Loader Grapple Truck in an amount not to exceed $224,587.

BACKGROUND
Illegal dumping is a serious problem that affects our community’s quality of life, finances,
and the environment. To better address illegal dumping and its negative impacts, the
Maintenance Division acquired a Petersen TL3 Lightning Loader in FY 2018-2019 from
reimbursement fees received from Waste Management as part of their Franchise
Agreement with the City. The lightning loader was the first step in establishing an Illegal
Dumping Program with dedicated equipment and staff, providing them with safer and
more efficient means to dispose of bulky trash and clean up illegal dumpsite materials.

While staff have been able to better respond to illegal dumping incidents, illegal dumping
continues to be a significant problem within the City. Since July 2019, there have been
over 2,700 work orders resulting in more than 5,000 tons of debris and trash being
collected by the Maintenance Division. Therefore, the purchase of a second Petersen TL3
Lightning Loader Grapple Truck will expand the Illegal Dumping Program and enable a
second crew to exclusively respond to incidents of illegal dumping throughout the City.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Purchase Order No. 20230005 with Nixon-Egli Equipment Company of
Southern California
July 20, 2022
Page 2

DISCUSSION
A new Petersen TL3 Lightning Loader Grapple Truck for the Illegal Dumping Program will
allow the Maintenance Division to double their efforts to address the increased and
growing problem of illegal dumping within the City. Currently, if additional crews are
assigned to assist in cleaning up illegal dumping sites and debris, they must do it
manually, which is a slow and cumbersome process. The addition of a second Lightning
Loader provides staff with a safer, more efficient method to pick up and haul illegally
dumped debris and large, heavier items (e.g., mattresses, appliances, furniture, etc.). It
will also allow two crews to be scheduled daily, which will improve response times to
citizen requests.

As part of the new solid waste agreement amendment with Waste Management, the City
will receive additional funds from Waste Management in the amount of $90,000 to fund
an Equipment Operator who will operate the Lightning Loader. The City will also receive
$200,000 from Waste Management as part of their regular Franchise Agreement fees to
address illegal dumping for the purchase of this equipment. Since the cost of the
equipment has increased from the original solid waste agreement negotiations, the City
will fund the remaining $25,000 for this purchase from savings realized from other fees
received from Waste Management.

The new 2021 Demo Unit Petersen TL3 Lightning Loader Grapple Truck, subject to this
Council action, will be acquired through Sourcewell Cooperative Contract No. 040621-
PII, as authorized in Palmdale Municipal Code §3.08.090. Sourcewell offers commodities,
products, and services at prices, which have been assessed to be fair, reasonable, and
competitive. Petersen Industries, Inc., the manufacturer of bulky waste collection
solutions, was awarded the Sourcewell Contract on May 26, 2021, and it continues
through July 2, 2025.

Staff recommends that the City Council approve Purchase Order 20230005 with Nixon-
Egli Equipment Company of Southern California.

FISCAL IMPACT
The Purchase Order amount for a new demo unit Petersen TL3 Grapple Lightning Loader
Truck will not exceed $224,587. Sufficient funds are budgeted in Fleet Maintenance
Account 15433007-734100.

  CONTRACT

  This Contract is between Sourcewell, 202 12th Street Northeast, P.O. Box 219, Staples, MN
  56479 (Sourcewell) and Petersen Industries, Inc., 4000 S.R. 60 W., Lake Wales, FL 33859

  Sourcewell is a State of Minnesota local government agency and service cooperative created
  under the laws of the State of Minnesota (Minnesota Statutes Section 123A.21) that offers
  cooperative procurement solutions to government entities. Participation is open to federal,
  state/province, and municipal governmental entities, higher education, K-12 education,
  nonprofit, tribal government, and other public entities located in the United States and Canada.
  Sourcewell issued a public solicitation for Bulk Solid Waste and Recycling Equipment from
  which Vendor was awarded a contract.

  Vendor desires to contract with Sourcewell to provide equipment, products, or services to
  Sourcewell and the entities that access Sourcewell’s cooperative purchasing contracts
  (Participating Entities).

  1. TERM OF CONTRACT

  A. EFFECTIVE DATE. This Contract is effective upon the date of the final signature below.

  B. EXPIRATION DATE AND EXTENSION. This Contract expires June 2, 2025, unless it is cancelled
  sooner pursuant to Article 22. This Contract may be extended up to one additional one-year
  period upon request of Sourcewell and with written agreement by Vendor.

  C. SURVIVAL OF TERMS. Articles 11 through 14 survive the expiration or cancellation of this
  Contract.

  2. EQUIPMENT, PRODUCTS, OR SERVICES

  A. EQUIPMENT, PRODUCTS, OR SERVICES. Vendor will provide the Equipment, Products, or
  Services as stated in its Proposal submitted under the Solicitation Number listed above.
  Vendor’s Equipment, Products, or Services Proposal (Proposal) is attached and incorporated

Resolution entitled “Annexation 14-433” with the County Sanitation District No. 14 of
Los Angeles County.

BACKGROUND
In accordance with the Revenue and Tax Code (Sections 99 and 99.01) any time there
is a jurisdictional change, the County Auditor is required to adjust the allocation of
property tax revenue for local agencies whose service area or service responsibility
would be altered by the jurisdictional change. This adjustment, or “Tax Sharing
Agreement” determines the distribution of the annual property tax among all affected
public agencies and special districts. In this case, the Copart Development located at
35th Street East and Ave. L-8 has requested annexation into the County Sanitation
District (CSD) No. 14. This annexation is a condition of the developments entitlement
and required prior to receiving sewer service.

DISCUSSION

In the attached letter dated August 10, 2020, the County Sanitation District has
requested that the City of Palmdale enter into a tax sharing agreement for the
annexation of parcel number 3170-015-007 as shown in Exhibit A, also known as the
Copart Development.

The execution of the attached Joint Resolution will approve the tax sharing agreement
by the City for the annexation of the subject property into the County Sanitation District
No. 14 boundary. All public agencies and special districts that receive property tax
revenues for this parcel execute and are a party to the same resolution.

Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-079 authorizing
the Mayor to execute the Joint Tax Sharing Resolution entitled Annexation No. 14-433
with the County Sanitation District No. 14 for the Copart Development.

FISCAL IMPACT
The current property tax share ratio for the City of Palmdale within the area of the
Copart Development property is 0.068146113 (6.8146%) This Council action will
allocate 0.000436142 (0.0436%) of the overall tax share to the County Sanitation
District No. 14 resulting in a net City tax share rate of 0.067709971 (6.7709%). For
example, a $10,000 increase in assessed value for a parcel will generate an additional
$100 in total property taxes. The City would receive $6.7709 as a condition of the tax
share and the Sanitation District would receive $0.0436142. This allocation is made in
accordance with the State Revenue and Taxation Code and the allocation formula is
established and calculated by the County Auditor-Controller.

  ANNEXATION NO. 433

  WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 99 and 99.01 of the Revenue and Taxation Code,
prior to the effective date of any jurisdictional change which will result in a special district
providing a new service, the governing bodies of all local agencies that receive an
apportionment of the property tax from the area must determine the amount of property
tax revenues from the annual tax increment to be exchanged between the affected
agencies and approve and accept the negotiated exchange of property tax revenues by
resolution; and

  WHEREAS, the governing bodies of the agencies signatory hereto have made
determinations of the amount of property tax revenues from the annual tax increments to
be exchanged as a result of the annexation to County Sanitation District No. 14 entitled
Annexation No. 433;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The negotiated exchange of property tax revenues resulting from the
annexation of territory to County Sanitation District No. 14 in the annexation entitled
Annexation No. 433 is approved and accepted.

  SECTION 2. For each fiscal year commencing on and after July 1, 2022, or after
the effective date of this jurisdictional change, whichever is later, the County Auditor shall
transfer to County Sanitation District No. 14 a total of 0.3355838 percent of the annual
 tax increment attributable to the land area encompassed within Annexation No. 433 as
shown on the attached Worksheet.

  SECTION 3. No additional transfer of property tax revenues shall be made from
any other tax agencies to County Sanitation District No. 14 as a result of annexation
entitled Annexation No. 433.

  SECTION 4. No transfer of property tax increments from properties within a
community redevelopment project, which are legally committed to a Community
Redevelopment Agency, shall be made during the period that such tax increment is
legally committed for repayment of the redevelopment project costs.

  SECTION 5. If at any time after the effective date of this resolution, the
calculations used herein to determine initial property tax transfers or the data used to
perform those calculations are found to be incorrect thus producing an improper or
inaccurate property tax transfer, the property tax transfer shall be recalculated and the
corrected transfer shall be implemented for the next fiscal year.

  The foregoing resolution was adopted by the Board of Supervisors of the County
of Los Angeles, the Board of Directors of County Sanitation District No. 14 of Los Angeles
County, and the governing bodies of Antelope Valley Cemetery District, Antelope Valley
Resource Conservation District, City of Palmdale, Antelope Valley – East Kern Water
Agency, and Antelope valley Mosquito and Vector Control District, signatory hereto.

  SECTION 6. The City Clerk shall certify to the adoption of this Resolution.

ISSUE
Award construction agreement with R.C. Becker and Son, Inc., for PN 761, Palmdale
Civic Center Complete Streets Project, in the amount of $6,405,637. for a term of 12

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Award construction Agreement No. A-7919 with R.C. Becker and Son, Inc., for
  PN 761, Palmdale Civic Center Complete Streets Project, in the amount of
  $6,405,637.

  2. Authorize the transfer of $2,210,600 of unappropriated Measure M Fund Balance
  into Account S0067209; and

  3. Authorize the Interim City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No.
  A-7919 with R.C. Becker and Son, Inc., including minimal and/or non-substantive
  changes.

BACKGROUND
Project No. 761, Palmdale Civic Center Complete Streets, provides for the complete
street improvements along 9th Street East and 10th Street East from Avenue Q-9 to
Avenue Q-12. Work includes construction of mini roundabouts, curb, gutter, accessible
ramps, and bus stations, upgrades to crosswalk striping and pavement markings,
sidewalk improvement, pavement reconstruction, street lighting, utility relocation, traffic
control plan development, and material certification submittals. All work will be
performed within the existing right of way. It is anticipated that construction will take
approximately twelve (12) months from the date the City issues the Notice to Proceed.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-071 approving Gun Dealer Permit 22-07 for Pung
  Whea Inc. doing business as Beeeft.

BACKGROUND
Gun Dealer Permit 22-07 is a request by Pung Whea Inc. to obtain a Gun Dealer’s
Permit for Beeeft located at 550 West Rancho Vista Boulevard, Suite G. Beeeft will
operate as a sporting goods store within a 1,200 square foot tenant space, with gun
sales being less than 30 percent of the overall sales. The applicant applied for a
business license on December 1, 2021, and has been operating as retail sales of
sporting goods only. On May 18, 2022, the applicant applied for the Gun Dealer Permit.

DISCUSSION
The Planning and Building & Safety Divisions reviewed and approved a Zoning Clearance
(Z22-264 application) determining that the above referenced business is located within
the Palmdale Trade and Commerce Center Specific Plan (SP). The property is
designated PD (Planned Development) within the SP. The SP Table 3: Land Use Matrix,
states that firearm sales are permitted if they are ancillary to a sporting goods store.
Beeeft will operate as a sporting goods store and gun sales will be an ancillary use. The
Building Official has reviewed the Zoning Clearance application and found the structure,

premises and equipment to conduct the business activity all comply with applicable
health, fire, building and safety laws of the State and the City.
The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department has reviewed the application, completed
background checks on the applicant and corporate directors, and has found that no false
statements have knowingly been made regarding the application for the Gun Dealer
Permit. Also, there are no criminal records for the applicant or corporate directors;
therefore, the Sheriff’s Department has recommended approval of Gun Dealer Permit
22-07.

The Federal Firearms application and the Gun Dealer Permit applications have been
completed and are on file in the Business License Division. The Gun Dealer Permit
requires City Council approval pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section
5.04.150. Upon approval of the Gun Dealer Permit the applicant will be able to obtain a
Federal Firearms License from the United States Department of Justice.

The applicant has demonstrated compliance with PMC Section 5.04.190 requirements
for the issuance of a Gun Dealer Permit. Therefore, it is recommended that City Council
adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-071 approving Gun Dealer Permit 22-07 with the following
condition:

    The applicant shall provide a copy of the Federal Firearms License prior to
  selling firearms and ammunition.

ISSUE

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-072 approving Entertainment Permit 22-08 and
  Dance Permit 22-09 for Lorocco’s Restaurant located at 1645 East Palmdale
  Boulevard, Suites G and H.

BACKGROUND
On April 8, 2021, the Planning Commission adopted Resolution No. PC-2020-036,
approving Conditional Use Permit 19-016, for Lorocco’s Restaurant to establish a Type
41 (On-Sale Beer and Wine) Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) License
and expand the existing restaurant to include a dance floor, stage area for live
entertainment and karaoke.

On June 2, 2022, Gilto Enterprises Incorporated, doing business as Lorocco’s
Restaurant, applied for Entertainment Permit 22-08 and Dance Permit 22-09, requesting
to provide live family entertainment such as karaoke, DJ’s, and small band ensembles,
with a dance floor not to exceed 30 percent of the gross floor area.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Resolution No. CC 2022-072-Entertainment Permit 22-08 and Dance Permit 22-09
July 20, 2022
Page 2

DISCUSSION
The provision of live entertainment and dancing, in conjunction with a bona fide restaurant
is permitted within the CC (Community Commercial) General Plan land use designation,
and C-3 (General Commercial) zone, subject to approval of Entertainment and Dance
Permits. The proposed use is beneficial and desirous to the community and is consistent
with the purpose, intent, and standards of the Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) and other
applicable ordinances and codes adopted by the City of Palmdale.

Lorocco’s is a bona fide restaurant that holds a Type 41 (On-Sale Beer and Wine) ABC
License with the primary use as sit-down dining. As specified within the conditions of
approval for CUP 19-016, the restaurant will not be conducting a bar or night club.
Entertainment and dance will consist of live family entertainment, karaoke, and small
band ensembles with designated dance floor space of 250 square feet, which is no more
than 30 percent of the gross area.

The hours of operation are Monday through Thursday from 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., and
Friday through Sunday from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 a.m. To maintain a safe environment for
its patrons, the restaurant is equipped with an on-site alarm system and security cameras,
as well as burglar and fire alarm systems.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department has reviewed the application, completed
background checks on the applicant and manager, and has found that no false
statements have knowingly been made regarding the application for the Entertainment
and Dance Permits. Also, there are no criminal records for the applicant or manager;
therefore, the Sheriff’s Department has recommended approval of Entertainment Permit
22-08 and Dance Permit 22-09.

Pursuant to PMC Sections 5.04.150 and 5.04.170, staff has authority to approve a Dance
Permit, however, an Entertainment Permit requires City Council approval. Given that the
Dance Permit is associated with the Entertainment Permit, the Director of Economic and
Community Development is recommending approval from the City Council.

Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-072 approving
Entertainment Permit 22-08 and Dance Permit 22-09 for Lorocco’s Restaurant with the
following conditions:

  1. All entertainment activities shall be conducted in compliance with PMC Chapter
  9.18.020. The operation of any sound amplifier or similar machine or device shall
  not be plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the building between the hours
  of 10:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m.

  2. Approval of a Manager’s Permit shall be required if the owner is not present during
  periods of live entertainment or dancing.

things, the urgency ordinance temporarily suspended the rules that would otherwise have
required that each planning commissioner be nominated by the councilmember
representing the particular district for which they were appointed to represent.

As a result of the urgency ordinance, the City Council has the option (but not the duty) to

   ARTICLE 1. OFFICES

  Section 1.1. Principal Office The principal office of The Palmdale Aerospace
Academy, Inc. (the “Corporation”) is hereby fixed and located at 38060 20th Street East, Palmdale,
CA 93550. The board of directors of the Corporation (the “Board”) shall have the full power and
authority to change the principal office from one location to another, and such location may
be at any place where the Corporation is qualified to conduct its activities. The Secretary shall
note any change of location of the principal office.

  Section 1.2. Other Offices. Branch or subordinate offices may be established at
any time by the Board at any place or places where the Corporation is qualified to conduct its
activities.

  ARTICLE 2. MEMBERSHIP

  Section 2.1. Members. The Corporation shall have no members within the
meaning of Section 5056 of the California Nonprofit Corporation Law. Any action that would
otherwise require approval by a majority of all members or approval by the members shall
require only approval of the Board. All rights which would otherwise vest in the members shall
vest in the Board.

  Section 2.2. Associates. Nothing in this Article 2 shall limit the right of the
Corporation to refer to persons associated with it as “members” even though such persons are not
members, and no such reference shall constitute anyone a member, within the meaning of
Section 5056 of the California Nonprofit Corporation Law. The Board may adopt policies and
procedures for the admission of associate members or other designated members who shall have
no voting rights in the Corporation, and such associate or other members shall not be “members”
of the Corporation as defined in Section 5056 of the California Nonprofit Corporation Law. The
Corporation may confer some or all of the rights of a member, as set forth in the California
Nonprofit Corporation Law, upon any person or persons who do not have the right to vote for or
regarding (i) the election of Directors, (ii) a disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of
the Corporation, (iii) a merger or dissolution of the Corporation, (iv) changes to the
Corporation’s Articles of Incorporation or Bylaws, or (v) the selection of delegates who possess
any of the preceding voting rights, but no such person shall be a member within the meaning of
Section 5056 of the California Nonprofit Corporation Law.

  ARTICLE 3. DIRECTORS

  Section 3.1. Powers. Subject to provisions of the California Nonprofit Public
Benefit Corporation Law and any other applicable laws and any limitations of the Articles of
Incorporation and these Bylaws, the activities and affairs of the Corporation shall be conducted
and all corporate powers shall be exercised by or under the direction of the Board. The Board
may delegate the management of the activities of the Corporation to any person or persons, a
management company or Committees however composed, provided that the activities and affairs
of the Corporation shall be managed and all corporate powers shall be exercised under the

LA1:1206318.11  1
  ultimate direction of the Board. Without prejudice to such general powers, but subject to the
 same limitations, it is hereby expressly declared that the Board shall have the following powers
 in addition to the other powers enumerated in these Bylaws:

  (a)  to select, remove, and supervise all the officers, agents and employees of
 the Corporation, prescribe qualifications, powers, and duties for them that are not inconsistent
 with law, the Articles of Incorporation or these Bylaws, fix their compensation, and require from
 them security or otherwise provide for faithful service;

  (b)  to conduct, manage and control the affairs and activities of the Corporation
 and to make such rules and regulations therefor not inconsistent with law, the Articles of
 Incorporation or these Bylaws, as they may deem best;

  (c)  to adopt, make and use a corporate seal and alter the form of the seal;

  (d)  to borrow money and incur indebtedness on behalf of the Corporation and
 cause to be executed and delivered for the Corporation’s purposes, in the corporate name,
 promissory notes, bonds, debentures, deeds of trust, mortgages, pledges, hypothecations, and
 other evidences of debt and securities therefor; and

  (e)  seek out and actively pursue outside resources and funding for the
 purposes of improving, maintaining or expanding the services provided by the Corporation.

  Section 3.2. Number of Directors. There shall be no more than twelve (12) directors
of the Board. As per section 3.3 there shall be nine (9) positions filled by the original designating
agencies. The Board reserves the right to fill and designate an additional three (3) “at large” directors
at its discretion without further notice except as provided by Government Code 54950 et. seq.

  Section 3.3. Selection and Term of Office.

  (a)  Designation of Directors. The directors of the Board (the “Directors”)
 shall be selected in the following manner: the Palmdale School District shall designate three (3)
 Directors, the City of Palmdale shall designate three (3) Directors, and the AERO Institute shall
 designate one (1) Director. By a majority vote of the Directors present and voting at the annual
 meeting of the Board, provided that a quorum is present, the Board shall elect one (1) Director
 employed in or with experience in the private sector in a field related to the areas of study
 emphasized at the Academy (as defined herein) (the “Private Sector Director”). The final
 Director shall be selected by the parent association (or the parent-teacher association, or the
 parent-teacher-student association, as applicable) of the Academy, subject to the approval of the
 Board (the “Parent Director”). The Board, or any committee of the Board so authorized, shall
 administer and oversee the appointment or approval, as applicable, of the Private Sector Director
 and the Parent Director to the Board.

  (b)  Term of Office. All Directors of the Corporation shall serve a term of
 three (3) years, expiring on July 31 of the third year of office, and shall hold office until the
 expiration of the term for which selected and until a successor has been duly designated, or until
 that Director’s earlier resignation or removal in accordance with these Bylaws and the California
 Nonprofit Corporation Law.
  The terms of the Directors shall be staggered, with the intention that only one-

 third (1/3) of the directors of the Board shall be selected each year to replace the one-third (1/3)
of the Directors whose terms shall expire each year. The Directors in the first election group
shall have their initial term as Director reduced to only one (1) year, and such Directors shall
include one (1) Director designated by the Palmdale School District, one (1) Director designated
by the City of Palmdale, and the Parent Director. The Directors in the second election group
shall have their initial term as Director reduced to only two (2) years, and such Directors shall
include one (1) Director designated by the Palmdale School District, one (1) Director designated
by the City of Palmdale, and the Director designated by the AERO Institute. The Directors in
the third election group shall have their initial term remain as three (3) years, and shall include
one (1) Director designated by the Palmdale School District, one (1) Director designated by the
City of Palmdale, and the Private Sector Director. With respect to the initial Directors appointed
by them, each of the Palmdale School District and the City of Palmdale shall determine which of
such initial Directors shall be allocated to each election group. If these Bylaws are amended to
alter the number of Directors comprising the Board, any increase or decrease in such number
shall be apportioned among the election groups so as to maintain the number of Directors in each
election group as nearly equal as practicable, and any additional Directors elected to fill a
vacancy resulting from an increase in any election group shall hold office for a term that shall
coincide with the remaining term of that election group.

  After the expiration of the initial terms of the Directors in each of the three (3)
election groups, all Directors in each election group shall serve terms of three (3) years. No
Director shall serve more than two (2) complete, consecutive three-year terms. A Director who
has served two (2) such consecutive three-year terms shall be eligible to serve again as a Director
after one (1) year has passed since the expiration of such Director’s last term of office.

  For purposes of this Section 3.3, any Director elected to serve an unexpired term
created by an existing vacancy on the Board (provided that the vacancy occurs during, rather than
prior to, such term and therefore such Director serves less than three (3) full years during his or
her initial term as a Director), or any Director whose initial term as a Director is less than three
years as a result of the initial staggering of the terms of Director positions as described in this
Section 3.3, shall be eligible to serve two (2) full three-year terms thereafter, regardless of the
length of time served in the unexpired term created by such vacancy or in such initial term.

  (c)  Selection Criteria. When selecting and designating Directors to the Board,
each designator shall be mindful of the benefits of the inclusion of Directors with expertise in
curriculum, instruction and assessment, finance, business management, special education, law
and facilities.

  The Parent Director shall be chosen from among the parents of students then
enrolled at the Academy. The Parent Director shall not be required to be the parent of a student
who will be enrolled at the Academy during the entirety of such Parent Director’s three (3) year
term, provided, however, that, if at any time during such Parent Director’s term, the child of the

 Parent Director ceases to be a student then enrolled in the Academy, the Parent Director shall be
deemed to have resigned from the Board, creating a vacancy under Section 3.4.

  Section 3.4. Vacancies.

  (a)  Events Causing Vacancies. A vacancy on the Board shall be deemed to
exist at the occurrence of any of the following:

  (i)  the death, resignation or removal of any Director;

  (ii)  the failure of the applicable designator to designate the number of
  Directors required to be designated at such time as a vacancy occurs;

  (iii)  with respect to the Parent Director, the deemed resignation of such
  Director upon the child of such Parent Director ceasing to be a student then enrolled in
  the Academy; or

  (iv)  the increase of the authorized number of Directors.

  (b)  Removal.

  (i)  Any Director may be removed, with or without cause, by a vote of
  a majority of the Directors then in office.

  (ii)  Any Director shall be removed automatically from the Board
  without any action required by the Board, if such Director has been declared of unsound
  mind by a final order of court, or convicted of a felony, or found by a final order or
  judgment of any court to have breached any duty under Chapter 2, Article 3 of the
  California Nonprofit Public Benefit Corporation Law.

  (iii)  No reduction in the authorized number of Directors shall effect a
  removal of any Director prior to the expiration of such Director’s term of office.

  (c)  Resignations. Any Director may resign, which resignation shall be
effective upon giving written notice to the Chairperson of the Board, the President (if any), the
Secretary or the Board, unless the notice specifies a later time for the effectiveness of such
resignation, provided that, except upon notice to the Attorney General of the State of California,
no Director may resign if the Corporation would then be left without a duly-elected Director or
Directors in charge of its affairs. If the resignation of a Director is effective at a future time, a
successor may be designated before that time, to take office when the resignation becomes
effective. In addition, unexcused absence of any Director from four (4) regular Board meetings
over a one (1) year period shall be deemed a resignation of such absent Director from the Board,
creating a vacancy to be filled as provided in Section 3.4(d). The determination of whether an
absence is excused or unexcused shall be made by the Chairperson of the Board.

  (d)  Filling of Vacancies. Vacancies in the Board shall be filled in the same
manner as the vacant position was last filled; that is, either by the same designator as the
designator who appointed the Director(s) whose office is vacant, if applicable, or by the Board of
Directors, if the Director(s) whose office is vacant was elected by the Board . Each Director so

 selected shall hold office until the expiration of the term of the replaced Director and until a
successor has been selected and qualified.

  Section 3.5. Place of Meeting.  Meetings of the Board shall be held at the
principal office of the Corporation. The Board may designate that a meeting be held at any place
within California that has been designated by resolution of the Board or in the notice of the
meeting provided that all meetings of the Board shall be called, held and conducted in
accordance with the terms and provisions of the Ralph M. Brown Act California Government
Code Sections 54950, et seq., as said chapter may be modified by subsequent legislation.

  Section 3.6. Regular Meetings. Regular meetings of the Board shall be held on
the third Monday of each month at 4:15 p.m. local time. The Board shall hold an annual meeting
for the purpose of organization, appointment of officers, election of such directors, if any, as
are to be elected by the Board in the applicable year, and the transaction of other business.
Annual meetings of the Board shall be held without call or notice on the first Wednesday of July
of each year at 4:00 p.m. local time; provided, however, that the Board may designate another
date or time for the annual meeting in any year. If for any reason the annual meeting is not
held on the date scheduled, the term of office for the incumbent directors and officers shall
continue until adjournment of the succeeding Board meeting at which such elections take place.
Notice of regular and annual meetings is not required if conducted in accordance with these
Bylaws. Agendas for each such meeting must be posted seventy-two (72) hours previous to such
meeting.

  All meetings of the Board shall be called, held and conducted in accordance with
the terms and provisions of the Ralph M. Brown Act California Government Code Sections
54950, et seq., as said chapter may be modified by subsequent legislation.

  Section 3.7. Special Meetings. Special meetings of the Board for any purpose or
purposes may be called at any time by the Chairperson of the Board or by a majority of the
Directors, or as otherwise provided by the terms and provisions of the Ralph M. Brown Act
California Government Code Sections 54950, et seq., as said chapter may be modified by
subsequent legislation.

  Notice of the time and place of special meetings, and the business to be transacted
at the meeting, shall be provided to the Directors and to all media who have provided written
notice to the Corporation. All notices shall provide such information and be given with at least
such notice as is required in accordance with the terms and provisions of the Ralph M. Brown
Act California Government Code Sections 54950, et seq., as said chapter may be modified by
subsequent legislation that is applicable to the type of meeting called.

  Section 3.8. Quorum and Action of the Board.

  (a)  Quorum. A majority of the Directors then in office (excluding non-voting
Directors) constitute a quorum of the Board for the transaction of business, except to adjourn as
provided in Section 3.11.

  (b)  Valid Board Actions. Every act or decision done or made by a vote of a
majority of the Directors present at a meeting duly held at which a quorum is present shall be

LA1:1206318.11  5
 regarded as the act of the Board, unless a greater number be required by law, by the Articles of
Incorporation, or by these Bylaws, including, without limitation, acts or decisions relating to (a)
approval of contracts or transactions in which a Director has a direct or indirect material financial
interest, (b) approval of certain transactions between corporations having common
directorships, and (c) creation of and appointments to Committees, and (d) indemnification of
Directors. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a meeting at which a quorum is initially present may
continue to transact business notwithstanding the withdrawal of Directors from the meeting, if
any action taken is approved by at least a majority of the required quorum for such meeting.

  Section 3.9. Participation in Meetings by Conference Telephone. Meetings of the
Board may be held by teleconference, provided that all Directors participating in the meeting
must be able to hear one another. All meetings held by teleconference must comply with the
terms and provisions of the Ralph M. Brown Act California Government Code Sections 54950,
et seq., as said chapter may be modified by subsequent legislation.

  Section 3.10. Waiver of Notice. Except as otherwise provided in the Ralph M.
Brown Act California Government Code Sections 54950, et seq. with respect to waivers of
notice of special meetings, notice of a meeting need not be given to any Director who signs a
waiver of notice or a written consent to holding the meeting or an approval of the minutes
thereof, whether before or after the meeting, or who attends the meeting without protesting, prior
thereto or at its commencement, the lack of notice to such Director. All such waivers, consents
and approvals shall be filed with the corporate records or made a part of the minutes of the
meetings. A waiver of notice need not specify the purpose of any regular or special meeting of
the Board. Directors can protest a lack of notice only by presenting a written protest to the
Secretary either in person, by first-class mail addressed to the Secretary at the principal office of
the Corporation as contained on the records of the Corporation as of the date of the protest, or by
facsimile addressed to the facsimile number of the Corporation as contained on the records of the
Corporation as of the date of the protest.

  Section 3.11. Adjournment. A Board meeting may be adjourned in accordance
with the provisions of the Ralph M. Brown Act California Government Code Sections 54950, et
seq., as said chapter may be modified by subsequent legislation.

  Section 3.12. Conduct of Meetings. Meetings of the Board shall be presided over
by the Chairperson of the Board, or, in his or her absence, the Treasurer or, in the absence of
each of these persons, by a chairperson chosen by a majority of the Directors present at the
meeting. The Secretary of the Corporation shall act as secretary of all meetings of the Board,
provided that, in his or her absence, the presiding officer shall appoint another person to act as
secretary of the meeting.

  All meetings of the Board shall be called, held and conducted in accordance with
the terms and provisions of the Ralph M. Brown Act California Government Code Sections
54950, et seq., as said chapter may be modified by subsequent legislation.

  Section 3.13. Fees and Compensation.  Directors shall not receive any
compensation for their service as Directors or as members of Committees of the Board; provided,
however, that any Director may receive advances or reimbursement of actual reasonable
expenses incurred by such Director in carrying out his or her duties as a Director or as

LA1:1206318.11  6
 a member of a Committee of the Board, as may be authorized by the Board. This Section 3.13
shall not be construed to preclude any Director from serving the Corporation in any other
capacity as an officer, agent, employee or otherwise, and receiving reasonable compensation for
those services, as may be authorized by the Board.

  Section 3.14. Restrictions on Interested Directors.  Not more than forty-nine
percent (49%) of the persons serving on the Board at any time may be Interested Persons. An
“Interested Person” is (a) any person currently being compensated by the Corporation for services
rendered to it within the previous 12 months, whether as a full-time or part-time employee,
independent contractor or otherwise; (b) any employee or officer of any corporation, or any
shareholder holding more than 3 percent of the shares in any corporation, or any partner or
employee of any partnership, that has rendered compensated services to the Corporation
within the previous 12 months; and (c) any brother, sister, ancestor, descendant, spouse, brother-
in-law, sister-in-law, mother-in-law, father-in-law, daughter-in-law or son-in-law of any person
described in clause (a) or (b) above. Any violation of the provisions of this paragraph shall not,
however, affect the validity or enforceability of any transaction entered into by the Corporation.

  Section 3.15. Rights of Inspection. Every Director shall have the absolute right
at any reasonable time to inspect and copy all books, records, and documents of every kind and
to inspect the physical properties of the Corporation.

  Section 3.16. Guests of Honor. From time to time the Board, or any Committee
so authorized, may place in nomination before the Board the names of individuals for election to
life terms as Guests of Honor in recognition of especially meritorious service to the
Corporation. The specific requirements and procedures for nomination and election shall be
established by the Board, or any Committee so authorized, provided that any Director who has
served at least one full term as the Chairperson of the Board or the President (if any) shall be
eligible for nomination to the status of Guest of Honor.

  Guests of Honor shall receive notice of and be permitted to attend all meetings of
the Board and all functions of the Board, unless the Board by resolution has determined that such
Guest of Honor shall be excluded from any such meeting, but shall not be deemed Directors and
therefore shall not (i) have voting power or any notice rights as a Director, (ii) have any
authority to act as a Director, or (iii) be counted for quorum purposes. There shall be no limit to
the number of Guests of Honor.

  Section 3.17. Non-liability of Directors. The Directors shall not be personally
liable for the debts, liabilities or other obligations of the Corporation.

  The personal liability (including personal liability to a third party for monetary
damages) of any Director for such person’s acts or omissions occurring within the scope of the
performance of such person’s duties as such shall be limited to the fullest extent permitted by
law (including Section 5047.5 of the California Nonprofit Corporation Law or Section 5239 of
the Nonprofit Public Benefit Law, as applicable). Such Directors shall also have a right to
indemnification by the Corporation as and to the extent set forth in Article 9 hereof.
